code.title: Complex Sum via Operator+
code.description:
Create a Complex class that stores a real part and an imaginary part and overloads the binary + operator so two complex numbers can be added with a simple + sign. Read two complex numbers, add them using the overloaded operator and print the result in standard a + bi form.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: real1 imag1 real2 imag2.

Output Format:
One line with the sum printed as '<real> + <imag>i' when the imaginary part is zero or positive, and '<real> - <imag>i' (with the positive magnitude of the imaginary part) when the imaginary part is negative.

Constraints:
-100 <= each integer <= 100

code.title: Wallet Balance with Operator+
code.description:
A digital wallet holds money as rupees and paise. Define a Money class and overload the + operator so two wallet balances can be added in one expression; a paise total of 100 or more must carry over into rupees. Print the combined balance.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: rupees1 paise1 rupees2 paise2.

Output Format:
One line: 'Total balance: Rs. <rupees>.<paise>' where the paise part is always shown as exactly two digits (zero padded).

Constraints:
0 <= rupees <= 100000, 0 <= paise <= 99

code.title: Vector Difference with Operator-
code.description:
Model a 2D displacement with a Vector2D class and overload the binary - operator so that a - b gives the difference vector (a minus b). Read two vectors and print the components of the difference.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: x1 y1 x2 y2.

Output Format:
One line with two integers separated by a single space: dx and dy, where dx = x1 - x2 and dy = y1 - y2.

Constraints:
-1000 <= each integer <= 1000

code.title: Fraction Product with Operator*
code.description:
Define a Fraction class with a numerator and a denominator and overload the * operator so two fractions multiply naturally. Read two fractions and print their product as p/q (the product is not reduced). Input Format: One line with four integers: num1 den1 num2 den2. Output Format: One line: '

/' where p = num1 * num2 and q = den1 * den2. Constraints: -100 <= numerator <= 100, 1 <= denominator <= 100 (denominators are positive; the product is printed unreduced)

code.title: Equal Volume Boxes with Operator==
code.description:
A warehouse compares cartons by volume. Define a Box class with length, width and height, overload the == operator to compare two boxes by volume, then read two boxes and report whether their volumes are equal.

Input Format:
One line with six integers: l1 w1 h1 l2 w2 h2.

Output Format:
One line: '1' if the two volumes are equal, '0' otherwise.

Constraints:
0 <= each dimension <= 100

code.title: Closer Point with Operator<
code.description:
Two friends stand at different points on a grid. Define a Point class, overload the < operator so that p < q means p is strictly closer to the origin than q (compare squared distances), read two points and report which one is closer.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: x1 y1 x2 y2.

Output Format:
One line: 'Point 1 is closer' if the first point has the strictly smaller squared distance from the origin, otherwise 'Point 2 is closer' (this includes the tie case).

Constraints:
-100 <= each coordinate <= 100

code.title: Shift Clock via Operator+
code.description:
A shift scheduler adds two shift durations. Define a Time class with hours and minutes and overload the + operator to add two times with normalization: a minute total of 60 or more carries into hours. Print the combined duration as hh:mm.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: h1 m1 h2 m2 (each minutes value is below 60).

Output Format:
One line: '<h>:<mm>' where the minutes are shown as exactly two digits (zero padded) and the hours are printed as-is (they may exceed 24).

Constraints:
0 <= hours <= 48, 0 <= minutes <= 59

code.title: Stock Merge via Operator+
code.description:
A store merges the stock of the same item arriving from two shelves. Define an Item class with a name and a quantity and overload the + operator so two Item objects merge into one whose quantity is the sum of both quantities. Print the merged stock.

Input Format:
One line with a name (a single word) and a quantity, then another name (a single word) and a quantity.

Output Format:
One line: 'Merged stock: <name1> <total>' where <name1> is the first item's name and <total> is qty1 + qty2.

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 100000

code.title: Distance Ledger with Operator+ and Operator-
code.description:
A carpenter measures lengths in metres and centimetres. Define a Distance class with metres and cm and overload both + and - with normalization (100 cm = 1 m). Read two distances and an operator character, then apply the requested operation.

Input Format:
One line with four integers m1 c1 m2 c2 followed by a character '+' or '-'.

Output Format:
One line: 'Result: <m> m <c> cm' with 0 <= c <= 99 after normalization.

Constraints:
0 <= metres <= 1000, 0 <= cm <= 99; for '-' the first distance is never smaller than the second

code.title: Heavier Item with Operator>
code.description:
A courier sorts parcels by weight. Define a Weight class with kilograms and grams and overload the > operator to tell which parcel is heavier. Read two parcels and report the heavier one.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: kg1 g1 kg2 g2.

Output Format:
One line: 'Item 1 is heavier' if the first weight is strictly greater than the second, otherwise 'Item 2 is heavier' (this includes the tie case).

Constraints:
0 <= kg <= 100, 0 <= g <= 999

code.title: Complex Accumulator with Operator+=
code.description:
An accounting program keeps a running complex total. Define a Complex class and overload += as a member function (so += updates and returns the object itself) together with == for comparison. Start from a given complex value, accumulate N more values with +=, then compare the accumulated sum with an expected value using ==.

Input Format:
One line with: r i (start complex), then N, then N pairs 'r i' (the values to accumulate), then r i (the expected complex value).

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Sum: <real> + <imag>i' when the imaginary part is zero or positive, 'Sum: <real> - <imag>i' with the positive magnitude when it is negative.
Line 2: 'Equal' if the accumulated sum equals the expected complex number, otherwise 'Not equal'.

Constraints:
-1000 <= each integer <= 1000, 0 <= N <= 10

code.title: Minute Hand with Pre-Increment
code.description:
A watchmaker tests a minute hand by nudging it forward one minute at a time. Define a Time class (hours, minutes) and overload the prefix ++ operator so it advances the time by exactly one minute; minutes carry into hours and hours wrap around modulo 24. Read a start time and the number of nudges, then print the time before and after applying ++ that many times.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: h m n.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Before: hh:mm' (hours and minutes always shown as exactly two digits, zero padded).
Line 2: 'After: hh:mm'.

Constraints:
0 <= h <= 23, 0 <= m <= 59, 1 <= n <= 300

code.title: Pretty Wallet with Stream Insertion
code.description:
A banking console wants balances printed in a fixed style. Define a Money class with rupees and paise, overload + to combine two balances (paise carry into rupees) and overload << as a friend function so that 'cout << amount' prints in the pretty 'Rs. r.pp' style. Read two wallets and print each one plus their combination.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: rupees1 paise1 rupees2 paise2.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Wallet 1: Rs. <r>.<pp>' (paise as exactly two digits).
Line 2: 'Wallet 2: Rs. <r>.<pp>'.
Line 3: 'Combined: Rs. <r>.<pp>'.

Constraints:
0 <= rupees <= 100000, 0 <= paise <= 99
code.output1:
Wallet 1: Rs. 999.99
Wallet 2: Rs. 1.01
Combined: Rs. 1001.00
code.output2:
Wallet 1: Rs. 50.50
Wallet 2: Rs. 50.50
Combined: Rs. 101.00
code.output3:
Wallet 1: Rs. 0.00
Wallet 2: Rs. 100.99
Combined: Rs. 100.99
code.sampleoutput1:
Wallet 1: Rs. 120.05
Wallet 2: Rs. 80.95
Combined: Rs. 201.00
code.sampleoutput2:
Wallet 1: Rs. 0.01
Wallet 2: Rs. 0.01
Combined: Rs. 0.02

code.title: Fraction IO Round Trip
code.description:
Build a Fraction class that knows how to read and print itself. Overload >> as a friend to read 'numerator denominator', << as a friend to print 'p/q', and + to add fractions; every printed fraction is reduced to lowest terms using gcd (the denominator stays positive, so the sign lives on the numerator). Input Format: One line with four integers: num1 den1 num2 den2 (denominators are positive). Output Format: Line 1: 'First:

/' (f1 reduced). Line 2: 'Second:

/' (f2 reduced). Line 3: 'Sum:

/' (f1 + f2 reduced; a zero fraction prints as 0/1 and an integer value keeps its /1). Constraints: -100 <= numerator <= 100, 1 <= denominator <= 100

code.title: Score Card with Subscript Operator
code.description:
A quiz platform stores five component marks for a contestant. Define a Score class that keeps the marks in an array and overloads the [] subscript operator so s[i] returns the i-th mark for 0 <= i <= 4, while any other index prints an out-of-range message. Read the five marks and a list of query indices, applying s[idx] for each query.

Input Format:
Line 1: five integers (the marks).
Line 2: an integer K.
Line 3: K query indices.

Output Format:
For each query, one line: 'Score <i>: <value>' for a valid index, or 'Score <i>: Invalid index' otherwise.

Constraints:
0 <= each mark <= 100, 1 <= K <= 10, -5 <= each query index <= 10
code.output3:
Score 2: 33
Score 5: Invalid index
Score -2: Invalid index
code.sampleoutput2:
Score 5: Invalid index
Score -1: Invalid index
Score 1: 60

code.title: Currency Match with Equality Operators
code.description:
An FX desk compares money across currencies using fixed integer rates: 1 USD = 83 INR and 1 EUR = 90 INR. Define a Currency class with a code and an amount, overload == to compare the INR values and != as the negation of ==. Read two currencies and report both checks.

Input Format:
One line with: code1 amount1 code2 amount2 (codes are INR, USD or EUR).

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Currency 1: <code> <amount>'.
Line 2: 'Currency 2: <code> <amount>'.
Line 3: 'Equality check: Same value' if == is true, otherwise 'Equality check: Different value'.
Line 4: 'Inequality check: Values differ' if != is true, otherwise 'Inequality check: Values match'.

Constraints:
0 <= amount <= 100000
code.output1:
Currency 1: INR 1000
Currency 2: USD 12
Equality check: Different value
Inequality check: Values differ
code.output2:
Currency 1: USD 0
Currency 2: INR 0
Equality check: Same value
Inequality check: Values match
code.output3:
Currency 1: EUR 2
Currency 2: EUR 2
Equality check: Same value
Inequality check: Values match
code.sampleoutput1:
Currency 1: USD 10
Currency 2: INR 830
Equality check: Same value
Inequality check: Values match
code.sampleoutput2:
Currency 1: EUR 5
Currency 2: USD 10
Equality check: Different value
Inequality check: Values differ

code.title: Polynomial Composer with Operators
code.description:
A symbolic math tool builds polynomials from coefficient lists. Define a Polynomial class (degree up to 10, integer coefficients stored from the constant term upward) and overload + to add two polynomials term by term and * with an integer scalar on the right to scale every coefficient. Read two polynomials and a scalar, then print their sum and the scaled first polynomial, skipping terms with zero coefficients (print 0 if nothing remains).

Input Format:
One line with: degA followed by degA+1 coefficients (constant first), then degB followed by degB+1 coefficients, then an integer scalar.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Sum: <polynomial>'.
Line 2: 'Scaled: <polynomial>'.
Polynomial formatting: terms are printed from the highest power down; every nonzero term is '<coef>x^k' (k >= 2), '<coef>x' (k = 1) or '<coef>' (k = 0), joined by ' + ' or ' - ' with absolute coefficient values; a leading negative prints as '-'; a coefficient of 1 or -1 omits the number before x; zero terms are skipped; the all-zero polynomial prints as '0'.

Constraints:
0 <= degree <= 10, -50 <= coefficient <= 50, -10 <= scalar <= 10

code.title: Matrix Studio with Operator Overloads
code.description:
A graphics course builds a tiny linear-algebra studio around a Matrix2x2 class. Overload + and - element-wise, * as true matrix multiplication, and << as a friend so that 'cout << m' prints both rows. Read two matrices and print their sum, difference and product.

Input Format:
One line with eight integers: a b c d e f g h, where the first matrix is [[a b] [c d]] and the second is [[e f] [g h]].

Output Format:
'Sum:' then the matrix (two lines, two integers per line separated by one space), then 'Difference:' with its matrix, then 'Product:' with its matrix.

Constraints:
-10 <= each element <= 10
code.whitelist: operator+, operator-, operator*, operator<<, friend, ostream

code.title: Big Integer Adder with Operator+
code.description:
Cryptography utilities often need arithmetic beyond 64-bit. Define a BigInt class that stores a non-negative decimal number as a string of digits (up to 40 digits) and overloads the + operator to perform school-book addition from the least significant digit with carries. Read two big integers, echo them and print the sum with no leading zeros.

Input Format:
One line with two decimal strings a and b (no leading zeros, length 1 to 40 each).

Output Format:
Line 1: 'A: <a>'.
Line 2: 'B: <b>'.
Line 3: 'Sum: <a + b>' with leading zeros removed (a sum of zero prints as 0).

Constraints:
1 <= length <= 40 digits, both values are non-negative

code.title: Calendar Advancer with Increment Operators
code.description:
A calendar service steps through dates one day at a time. Define a Date class and overload both ++ operators: prefix (++d) and postfix (d++) must each advance the date by one day, handling month lengths (30, 31, 28) and leap-year Februaries (years divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400), rolling over months and years. Read a start date and N, then print the sequence of N+1 dates, advancing with prefix ++ on odd steps and postfix ++ on even steps.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: dd mm yyyy n (the start date is a valid calendar date).

Output Format:
N+1 lines, each 'dd-mm-yyyy' with dd and mm shown as exactly two digits (zero padded), starting with the given date and then every advanced date.

Constraints:
1900 <= yyyy <= 2100, 1 <= n <= 60
